Area.evidence_source: All participants reported struggling to form and maintain romantic relationships. Since intimate trusting relationships were avoided by participants, intimacy was a relatively unknown experience and relationship crises frequently precipitated the wish to kill themselves. Andrew explained that the marital difficulties of his parents contributed to his avoiding 'emotional attachments' with women. Mark and Johan reported that breaking up with their partners was one of the factors contributing to their becoming suicidal. Johan said: That feeling of a girl leaving you like that. It is a feeling of you don't feel good enough, you don't feel sufficient, or you are not man enough and suddenly once again you feel ashamed of yourself. You are disappointed in yourself, why can't you just hold onto a girl. Mark and Brian discovered in their early adolescence that they are sexually attracted to other men. Growing up in a social context with powerful expectations of heterosexuality, they chose not to disclose their sexual orientation. This led them to experience profound feelings of isolation and exclusion and an 'identity crisis'. During this difficult time Mark and Brian took on the identity of being 'emo'. They described 'emo' as an emotional state of 'not being your happy self', 'just feel very down', 'feel up for nothing' and 'feel tired', They led an isolated existence, including 'wanting to be away from people' and 'not being accepted by anybody'. Mark and Brian explained that their wish to die was intricately connected with not being able to 'live [their] gayness' and believing that their pain was invisible to others. Through suicidal behaviour they hoped to make their pain visible: Imagine being a thirteen year old boy and you thinking about things that are sort of taboo and your brothers are sort of Jocks and stuff, and you have these thoughts which you don't want to have and I felt trapped, I felt angry and that's why I did suicide also. (Mark) I hate myself, you know, cos what is this! Not even God will accept me … many churches are obviously against homosexuality and it's like, I'm standing here and everyone is going crazy for God and there is a person with pain in the middle, who wants to commit suicide. You know, and nobody even sees that. That kind of was very contradictory for me. (Brian)
